items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: In the brass section they had the Leo Deja on trumpet

ctx.x: You never did join the WPA band then?

No, I was going to say, I always thought that was a little too slow money for me. I, I, well I should have because there wasn't nothing to it, you know. Most of the guys got in just for the money of it, you see. But like I say, then I was doing a little range, I was selling arrangements around you and everything, you know. But I, I, in other words, I was doing it just as good as those guys there, you see. So, and then another thing I, I didn't like it because the time that, like, you would get a good job, it…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: So he asked me would I join them because he had heard that I wasn't with Sidney.

ctx.x: I was staying on La Hop, La Hop and La Prusse, I believe it was, and Randy was staying right across the street from me. So, well like I said, at that time in working with the big band, I'd always work with some guys with maybe two or three pieces like Ryan Young and Frank's Quarter when the big band wasn't doing nothing. And I was doing a little range in that time for the band. Yeah. So when the word got around and Sidney had let me go, well, I remember Leo Dazio came to my house because he had one of the guys…
